newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ruehe sees Eurofighter decision in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Ruehe sees Eurofighter decision in first quarter.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Tuesday he expected parliament to approve plans to buy the Eurofighter early this year, enabling production of the jet fighter to go ahead on schedule.

Ruehe told German Radio parliament would make a decision "in the first quarter". He said delivery of Germany's batch of Eurofighters must begin by 2002 in order to phase out military aircraft which will be up to 40 years old by then.

Ruehe reached a price agreement last week with Daimler-Benz AG unit DASA, German contractor in the four-country Eurofighter partnership. The other partners are British Aerospace, Italy's Alenia and CASA of Spain.
DASA chief executive Manfred Bischoff confirmed on Monday that a price deal had been struck for Germany's planned order of 180 Eurofighters, but he declined to give details.
German media have speculated that the final cost of the planes would be between 20 billion ($12.6 billion) and 24 billion marks, down from DASA's original asking price of 26 billion marks.
Ruehe has struck an agreement with Finance Minister Theo Waigel to split the startup costs of Eurofighter production between the defence ministry and the general federal budgets.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.589 German Marks)
